Ternus told CNBC's MacKenzie Sigalos that Apple's growth came in spite of supply constraints and foreign exchange headwinds. "I think at this point, with everything we've achieved, it just feels like we've never been more confident that the best is yet to come," Ternus said. Palantir Technologies — Palantir shares were down 2% even after the company's third-quarter earnings topped Wall Street's estimates. Revenue for the period nearly doubled from a year earlier and surpassed $2 billion for the first time. The company's U.S. commercial revenue jumped 148% to $984 million, topping U.S. government revenue of $953 million. Palantir is also projecting about $2.65 billion in fourth-quarter revenue and $8.53 billion for full-year 2026. Lattice Semiconductor — The company's stock jumped 8% after Lattice solidly outpaced third-quarter revenue estimates and raised its forecast for the year. The semiconductor designer expects fourth-quarter revenue of between $325 million and $345 million, above the $293 million LSEG consensus estimate, and anticipates it will earn 82 cents to 86 cents per share after adjustments, topping the consensus estimate of 64 cents per share. The Clorox Company — The maker of Clorox Disinfecting Wipes added 2% after fiscal first-quarter results came in ahead of estimates. The company earned $1.55 per share on an adjusted basis on revenue of $1.91 billion. Analysts surveyed by LSEG were looking for $1.07 a share and $1.88 billion. Organic sales growth for the period also topped estimates. On Semiconductor — Shares fell about 2%. On Semiconductor said it would acquire Ferric, a maker of power converters, for $600 million in cash, plus up to $175 million in contingent consideration if certain revenue milestones are reached. Separately, the company said it expects fourth-quarter adjusted earnings in a range of 95 cents to $1.07 per share, while analysts polled by LSEG called for 95 cents per share. Apple — Apple shares were down 2% in extended trading after the consumer tech giant rolled out a disappointing margin forecast and iPad sales in the fiscal fourth quarter missed the Street's estimates. Fabrinet – The provider of advanced optical packaging jumped more than 10% after current-quarter guidance trounced the Street's estimates. Fabrinet sees second-quarter adjusted earnings in a range of $4.77 to $4.92 per share on revenue of $1.6 billion to $1.65 billion. Analysts were looking for $4.43 a share and $1.48 billion, per FactSet. Ibotta — The digital consumer promotions company gained 13% after its fourth-quarter guidance beat analysts' expectations. Ibotta sees revenue in a range of $94 million to $98 million, beating the FactSet consensus estimate of $93.4 million. Adjusted EBITDA also topped expectations. headlines.article_text: Palantir (PLTR) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Palantir reported Q3 earnings that topped Wall Street's estimates. U.S. commercial revenue more than doubled and surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time. The company has seen a boost from heightened demand for artificial intelligence tools. In this article PLTR Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:24 01:24 Palantir beats on earnings and revenue, Q3 commercial revenue surpasses government revenue Closing Bell: Overtime Palantir beat Wall Street's third-quarter estimates after the bell on Monday, with U.S. commercial revenue topping government for the first time as businesses adopt more of the company's artificial intelligence tools. Shares dipped about 3% in extended trading. Here's how the company did compared to LSEG estimates: Earnings per share : 44 cents adjusted vs. 41 cents expected Revenue : $2.31 billion vs. $2.18 billion expected Revenue nearly doubled from a year ago and blew past $2 billion for the first time ever, Palantir said. Net income more than doubled to $1.13 billion, or 44 cents per share, from about $476 million, or 18 cents per share. "I don't believe anyone's had consistent results like this in the history of software AI, ever," CEO Alex Karp told CNBC's Seema Mody in an interview, adding that the business is succeeding without salespeople. Palantir has long been known for its strength in the government sector, but its commercial segment caught up in Q3. U.S. commercial revenue jumped 148% to $984 million, surpassing U.S. government revenue of $953 million, which was up 96%. The company's U.S. commercial revenue has more than quintupled over the last two years. Palantir lifted its guidance, saying it now expects U.S. commercial revenue "in excess of" $3.56 billion for the full year. Last quarter, the company boosted its forecast to $3.42 billion. The company projects about $2.65 billion in revenue for the fourth quarter and about $8.53 billion for full-year 2026. Karp has openly supported the use of open-weight models and criticized leading AI labs, which he told CNBC earlier this year are forcing businesses to sell their data sovereignty. Karp, on Monday, also reiterated recent calls to nationalize AI labs, calling it the "only realistic way" to manage liability. In September, Karp joined major tech CEOs at the White House as calls for regulation mounted following claims from AI researchers that the technology has a more than 10% of killing humanity . "My message to everybody is: Beware of thinking you can delay the future in AI," he told CNBC. "The future is here. The political ramifications of it are here." Palantir stock chart.
